newsitem.title: HUNGARY: COFINEC H1 MARGINS DOWN YEAR-ON-YEAR.
newsitem.headline: COFINEC H1 MARGINS DOWN YEAR-ON-YEAR.

text.p: French-registered and Budapest-listed packaging materials company Cofinec S.A. reported a rise in consolidated first half pre-tax profits on Thursday but said operating margins fell year-on-year.

The operating profit margin slipped to 6.0 percent in the first half of 1997 compared with 6.6 percent in the same period a year ago, but was a "significant improvement" over the January-December 1996 margin of 1.3 percent, the company said in a statement.

Cofinec said pre-tax profits rose to 10.5 million French francs ($1.7 million) from 6.1 million in the same period of 1996, supported by net income from non-recurring items and lower net interest expenses. Operating profit, however, fell to 21.4 million French francs in the first six months of the year from 22.3 million.
Net sales grew to 355.4 million from 336.5 million with exports accounting for 11.1 percent or 39.3 million of the total, up from 33.9 million in the first half of 1996.

Cofinec, which operates in Hungary, the Czech Republic and Poland, said around 93 percent of export sales were contributed by its two Hungarian units, Petofi and Kner. Its Czech Krpaco unit accounted for the remaining seven percent.
In July, Cofinec merged the two Hungarian companies under the new banner of Confinec Hungary Rt.
Cofinec added that Krpaco experienced a decrease in order volumes in the first half of 1997 due to a "less favourable", Czech business environment.
Meanwhile, Cofinec Polska continued to show dramatic improvement in production efficiency during this period, although growth lagged behind plans, the company said.
"Sales and new customer business are increasing steadily, although not as quickly as expected," it said.
-- Emese Bartha, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040 ($ = 6.179 French Francs)
